claim: A practitioner backtest on SPY finds dealer gamma exposure (GEX) has a raw rank correlation of about -0.36 with next-day realized volatility, but the relationship falls to about -0.03 (not significant) after controlling for VIX and ATM implied volatility.

evidence.quote: After controlling for VIX and ATM IV, the GEX-only signal drops from rank correlation -0.36 (strong) to -0.03 (statistical noise, p=0.18).

claim: In 2008, forward 30-day realized volatility rose above the VIX from July until November, when the VIX caught up, and the VIX then overshot realized volatility in early 2009; in panics the VIX lags the onset of volatility and then overreacts.

evidence.quote: In July 2008, realized volatility on a 30-day, forward-looking basis began to spike over the VIX. This continued until November 2008 when the VIX finally caught up and matched realized volatility.
VIX is slow to react to the oncoming volatility and then overreacts once it realizes the volatility that is coming.

claim: Man Group's study of the top 20 VIX spikes over 30 years found mixed subsequent S&P 500 returns: when the index rose in the week after the spike, the second week was negative on average.

evidence.quote: However, the pattern reverses if the S&P 500 declines in the week after the VIX spike, as we saw between 29 November and 3 December. In this instance, returns persistence after the second week improves to 86%

claim: According to an IVolatility vendor analysis, single-day SPY implied-volatility spikes of 5 points or more were followed by an average SPY gain of about 5.12% over the next 20 trading days, roughly five times the baseline, using overlapping windows.

evidence.quote: IV spikes of ≥5 points in a single day were followed by an average +5.12% over 20 days — five times the baseline return.

claim: A reversal strategy on E-mini S&P 500 futures on FOMC announcement days, trading from 13:50 ET to the close against the prior 24-hour return, averaged about 0.18% net per announcement with a Sharpe ratio of 0.36 over October 1997 to January 2020 (180 announcements).

evidence.quote: A reversal strategy trading E-mini S&P 500 from 13:50 EST to the close, opposite the prior 24-hour return, averaged 0.18% net per FOMC announcement with Sharpe ratio 0.36 (Oct 1997–Jan 2020; 180 announcements; trades at bid/ask).
